In the current state (6/15/2020) I cannot recommend the Steam release of this game. It is a known issue that the Origin overlay causes frame rate issues with Mass Effect 3. If you own the game on Origin that is fine because you can disable the overlay there. Attempting to disable the overlay in Origin with the Steam release does not have the same effect. Regardless of what you do, the Origin overlay is still enabled when launching the Steam version. This causes random frame stutters from 60 to 30 fps. This also causes the mouse to stutter making looking around nauseating.

I was looking forward to playing this game but in the current state it is borderline unplayable. If the issue is fixed I would happily leave a glowing review as I am a big fan of the Mass Effect series.

Eight years later, and the Mac-n-Trash Walters Plagiarism-fest of Blatant Knockoffs & Corporate Numbskullery finally makes it to Steam. This is the game that inspired my oft-used phrase, "still a better ending than Mass Effect got." Think of the worst endings that narrative-driven games have received in the last 8 years, and *none* of them are as bad as this RGB nonsense.

Thing is, I got over the insanely absurd ending seven years ago. Much as I like to complain, it's really not the core of my issue with ME3. The thing I will never forgive the high-&-mighty, hypocritical, self-aggrandising egomaniac Mac-n-Trash Walters for is what he did to what was otherwise an amazing Sci-Fi universe. It wasn't just the ending, and it wasn't just ME3. His ego trashed ME2 as well. Either the story of the Collectors was shoe-horned in at the last minute of drawing board staging, or it was sent BACK to the drawing board part-way through development. Either way, you can easily tell if you know what to look for.

Anyone who remembers pre-patch ME3 will recall the fact that Kai Leng was nothing more than a blatant in-your-face Adam Jensen ripoff. But that was far, FAR from the only incident of shameless plagiarism that Walters is responsible for. There are countless lesser-known things that Walters plagiarised, such as the Chiggs. Those aren't protheans you're looking at. Javik is not a prothean. They're all a stolen model from a 90s military Sci-Fi show called Space: Above & Beyond. So I don't call the From Ashes squadmate Javik, I call him Chiggy von Richthofen. I don't care if the series wasn't so great, it's still plagiarism - and we all know what EA has to say about plagiarism. That is, of course, unless it's EA getting away with plagiarism - then they're perfectly hunky-dory about it. Whatever.

But when Mac-n-Trash Walters found himself on the receiving end of justified gamer-rage for how he screwed over the Mass Effect fanbase by making the ending so pointless... did he say anything indicative of him being a responsible adult capable of self-reflection or even the smallest modicum of humility? No. Instead, he said his critics were "ruining art" for criticising him. Yes, ruining art. All of it. Something which has been around since long before recorded history, before the first vestiges of the written word itself, all of "art-dom" was somehow 'ruined' by people daring to criticise his absolute trash-quality writing and story design.

The "man" has not created a single work of art his entire life. Everything he takes credit for is the work of someone else. Everything. Every idea, every concept, every little "once upon a time" sentence he has ever written has been the product of another's mind entirely. 

Walters' nonsense was bad enough, but Drew K. only made things worse by excusing and defending him to the point of self-deprecation. DK even went so far as to say that all his original ideas were "half-baked," and that he was somehow glad that Walters "rescued" things thereafter. What a pile of thresher dung. Mass Effect could have been so much more if not for the inhumanly toxic and megalomanaical corporate culture of EA.

So why did I finally buy this heap of hot garbage? Two reasons: 
1) Despite the best efforts of Mac-n-Trash Walters, the game is still somewhat enjoyable. This is especially so when using a combination of ALOT, EGM, TRM, and LIME+CEM. That latter duo makes the ending a less painful pill to swallow as well, and does so without breaking anywhere *near* as much lore as Walters tore apart. So there's that.
2) It may have taken over eight years for EA to stop throwing their little temper tantrum after not being able to nickle-and-dime people via hidden paywalls behind Valve's back, but at least they're finally doing the right thing. Sort of. So just like DA2 and DAI, I am buying everything I otherwise would have bought if EA had never ragequit Steam.

( Disclaimer: It's not that I'm loyal to Steam. But we didn't see Ubisoft pulling out back then, did we? )

But can I honestly recommend it to someone who has never played Mass Effect, or has yet to experience the travesty that is ME3? 

Yes. Feel my pain. Understand what it is like to have hundreds of hours of your gaming time completely wasted by the result of egocentric, lazy, unintelligent blow-hards being in charge of otherwise talented and creative people. The real creators who actually make this franchise worth something despite the best efforts of those at the top doing everything they can to utterly ruin it - THEY do not deserve to share the shame of what happened to Mass Effect. That is one of the ONLY two reasons I am not giving this a thumbs-down. 

Plus, until you've gone through this entire trilogy yourself, you cannot truly know how insulting it is to have that final piece of pyjak-dung flung in your face by a lazy, weak, and unintelligent batarian who thinks he's a better artist than Forta.

For anyone considering buying this game in order to circumvent having Origin on their system, don't bother. This title requires the Origin launcher to be installed and must be linked to an active Origin account. Origin launcher must continue running the entire time the game is open and closing origin mid-session will kill the game immediately.

I should have expected this. I've requested a refund immediately, and I recommend you save your money.

I went into Mass Effect 3 expecting a powerful conclusion to one of the greatest sci-fi trilogies in gaming. What I got was a rushed, inconsistent finale that undermines much of what made the first two games special.

Cons

- - - The Ending (Yes, That Ending)
After dozens of hours building relationships, making morally complex decisions, and shaping the fate of entire species, the finale boils down to a handful of color-coded choices that barely reflect your journey. It feels disconnected from the trilogy’s core theme: that your choices matter.

- Reduced RPG Depth
Compared to earlier entries, dialogue options and role-playing feel streamlined to the point of being shallow. Paragon/Renegade is still there, but many conversations feel like you're being railroaded.

- Questionable Writing Decisions
Some long-running character arcs either get sidelined or wrapped up too quickly. Emotional moments are there, but they often feel rushed rather than earned.

- War Asset System = Illusion of Control
The “galactic readiness” mechanic makes you grind side content and (at launch) multiplayer to get the “best” ending — which still doesn’t meaningfully change the outcome.

- Day-One DLC Controversy
Locking a squadmate behind DLC on release left a bad taste. It felt less like extra content and more like cut content sold separately.

- - - EA launcher
Still has LOTS of issues and makes running this game almost impossible.

Pros

+ Combat Is the Best in the Trilogy
Gunplay feels tight, abilities are more fluid, and biotic combos are incredibly satisfying. The faster pacing makes encounters more exciting than ever.

+ Some Incredible Emotional Moments
Certain story arcs — especially involving major alien races — deliver powerful payoffs. When the writing hits, it really hits.

+ Strong Voice Acting
The performances (especially for Shepard and key squadmates) carry many scenes that might otherwise fall flat.

+ Great Soundtrack
The music adds genuine weight to major scenes and elevates the atmosphere.

Final Thoughts

Mass Effect 3 isn’t a terrible game in isolation. In fact, mechanically it’s arguably the strongest entry. But as the conclusion to a trilogy built on choice, consequence, and player agency? It drops the ball HARD.

Recommended? YES but IF you buy the the legendary edition. 'Cause the fix the launcher problem and you get to enjoy all 3 games in one.

I was excited to see ME3 come to steam and WAS resigned to the fact that I'd probably have to re-buy the DLC. Then I saw that ME3 requires you to link your steam and origin. If I have to link my account anyway, then why should I have to repurchase DLC I've already bought? I still love this game, flaws and all, but I resent EA once again going out of their way to extract every dime they can from customers who have already paid for their products.
In addition, the fact that origin is still required to play is ridiculous. My excitement for the game coming to steam was partially due to the notion that I would finally be able to get rid of origin, as I only use it for this game and one other. If I was buying a completely new and unlinked copy of ME3 (and dlc) then the price would be completely fine to me, but it requires linking an account on which I already own the game and, therefore, is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

So I give this a positive rating because I still enjoy it despite its faults. With that said, FORCING us to use Origin is just stupid. However, I'm willing to bet that was EA's call. On the other hand, the controls are hot garbage since this game was very obviously designed for controllers yet won't let you use one and that is inexcusable (at time of review and as far as I am aware). People mention frame rate issues that I haven't seen, but I'll still caution you if that's a deal breaker. EA servers are still EA servers so there will be connection issues every so often. If you've invested a lot of time in another version of the game then I'll go ahead and warn you that your progress won't transfer over so don't expect it. If you love and grew up with Mass Effect like I did, you won't be turned off. It's still fun and I enjoy playing it with my brother and nephews, but faults MUST be pointed out in order to grow. If you get it, I'll see you on the Normandy.
EDIT: So I've started bumping into the issue of EA and Steam either telling me I don't own the game or just flat out not loading it up at all. Be careful if you plan on bothering with this. Honestly if you're curious, just wait for the Legendary Remaster (assuming it even comes out on steam which I doubt)
